content.comment_body: I'm updating my project from an older [product_name] [version_no] to a newer [version_no]. I use the operator device interface to adjust values up or down. The calculation for this is: new value = old value + (sign * gain) + initial value (similar to: a := a + 1) Where sign is either -1 or +1, and gain can be 1, 10, or 100. This worked fine on my previous [version_no]. However, when rewriting the software and adding features, I now encounter an error: "Circular reference is not allowed" when trying to link references together. I've attached screenshots to illustrate the issue. Is there any workaround besides going back to the old project version (i.e., upgrade the program from [version_no] to [version_no] while keeping circular references, and add new features afterward)? Best regards, [user_name]
You can use the Max or Min block to avoid circular references. See attachment.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is facing a logic issue after upgrading from an older to a newer [product_name] [version_no]. The updated hardware does not support circular references for value calculations, leading to an unexpected error that interrupts feature enhancements and usability. The issue stems from differences in how logic is processed between hardware versions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that logic operations such as circular referencing will remain compatible when transferring projects to newer hardware versions, making migration seamless without needing to change their logic structure.
